theme: PCMB against the published results of its paper on samples of the Alarm and Pigs networks, every node a target; GS, Fast-IAMB, and HITON-PC against bnlearn on the papers' networks and on linear-Gaussian graphs, every node a target; CMB against global PC read at the target on its paper's Alarm setting, every node a target
build: PCMB: Andrey pre-release build of 12 November 2026 (the 0.18.0 release branch with pcmb and its bounded subset listing as merged; the test's degrees of freedom of Spirtes et al. ran as a patch that returned the same sets and test counts as the merged default degrees_of_freedom='nonempty' on the 126 fits compared, every Alarm dataset and 6 Pigs datasets) | GS, Fast-IAMB, and HITON-PC: Andrey pre-release builds of the 0.18.0 release branch: 12 November 2026 for fast_iamb and hiton_pc as merged, 13 November 2026 for gs, whose shrink starts again from the first member after each removal | CMB: Andrey pre-release build of 13 November 2026 (the 0.18.0 release branch as merged with LOAD's skeleton step); the release branch of 14 November 2026, with exact upper-tail p-values, gave the same answers and test counts at every target of the 3 datasets rerun
verdict_rule: PCMB: no reference implementation exists, so each row sets Andrey's mean beside the paper's mean and standard deviation (Table 6), and the release card judges no row better or worse. The floor: per dataset, the mean over the targets of the errors minus the empty set's; a row passes when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of the mean difference lies wholly below 0 over at least 10 datasets, and the per-dataset differences are in the row | GS, Fast-IAMB, and HITON-PC: per cell (network or Gaussian graph, rows; 20 datasets, every node a target): per dataset, the mean over the targets with a nonempty true set of the distance of the set's precision and recall from (1, 1) (an empty answer counts precision 1, distance 1) and of the set's F1; D = Andrey's minus bnlearn's per dataset; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of the mean D lies wholly on the worse side of 0 (10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0)), better when wholly on the better side, a tie otherwise. A cell worse on seeds 0-19 on either measure was rerun on seeds 20-39 and is worse only when the fresh seeds agree; a cell better on seeds 0-19 was not rerun | CMB: no reference implementation exists, so each row sets Andrey's means beside the paper's (Table 1) and judges CMB against two global PCs read at the target, Andrey's pc with the same test and level and bnlearn 5.2.1 pc.stable with mi-adf: the mean over paired datasets of CMB's total minus the other's with its 95% percentile-bootstrap interval, better or worse when the interval lies wholly on that side of 0 over at least 10 datasets, on seeds 0-19, and a cell worse there counts only when it is worse again on seeds 20-39. The floor: per dataset, the total minus the empty answer's; a row passes when its interval lies wholly below 0
fit_protocol: PCMB: each fit in a fresh process on one core with one BLAS thread, every node of a dataset a target in one fit, no warm-up, a cap of 14,400 s per fit, past which a fit is a timeout and never scored; no fit failed or timed out. G-square tests at alpha 0.01 with no limit on the conditioning set; columns that hold one value are left out of the fit and answer the empty set, scored against the full network | GS, Fast-IAMB, and HITON-PC: each fit in a fresh process on one core with one BLAS thread, every node of a dataset a target in one fit, no warm-up, a cap of 1,800 s per fit, past which a fit is a timeout and never scored | CMB: each fit in a fresh process on one core with one BLAS thread, CMB once per target and each PC once per dataset, read at every target; no warm-up, a cap of 1,800 s per fit, past which a fit is a timeout and never scored; no fit failed or timed out. G-square tests at alpha 0.02 with no limit on the conditioning set, CMB with HITON-MB, its default blanket learner
error_metric: PCMB: distance: the mean over a dataset's targets with a nonempty answer of the distance of the set's precision and recall from (1, 1), the reading of the comparison with the paper: an empty answer has no precision or distance and counts in the recall as 0; distance_one counts an empty answer as distance 1; precision is the mean over the targets with an answer and recall the mean over all targets. The floor uses the set's errors, missing plus extra members, against the empty set's, the true set's size; every value is a mean over the row's datasets, and andrey_s is the median wall time of a fit for every target | GS, Fast-IAMB, and HITON-PC: set_distance: the mean over the targets of the distance of the set's precision and recall from (1, 1); set_f1_loss: 1 minus the mean over the targets of the set's F1. The floor uses the set's errors, missing plus extra members (the wrong answers of andrey.metrics.target_answer_scores), against the empty set's, the true set's size | CMB: total: per target, the edges at the target missing or extra against the true CPDAG plus those whose direction differs from it, an edge the CPDAG directs and the answer leaves undirected included (reversed); a dataset's value is the mean over its targets. lenient leaves out the undirected ones. The floor uses the total against the empty answer's, the target's degree
complete_definition: PCMB: true when every row has at least 10 datasets (the paper's number) | GS, Fast-IAMB, and HITON-PC: true when every row has at least 10 paired datasets (both fitted) | CMB: true when every row has at least 10 paired datasets
seeds_note: PCMB: Alarm rows hold 20 datasets, seeds 0-19, the first 10 the paper's number and 10 fresh; Pigs rows hold 10 datasets, seeds 0-9 | GS, Fast-IAMB, and HITON-PC: every cell holds 20 datasets, seeds 0-19; a rerun holds 20 fresh datasets, seeds 20-39 | CMB: every cell holds 20 datasets, seeds 0-19, and 20 fresh datasets, seeds 20-39

regimes.network_tables: net:<network>:<rows>: forward samples of the Alarm (37 variables) or Pigs (441) network's own tables, the columns in an order drawn from the seed, columns that hold one value left out of the fit
regimes.discrete: net:<network>:<rows>: forward samples of the bnlearn repository network, columns that hold one value left out of every fit, each answering the empty set at its target, every set scored against the whole network
regimes.gaussian: gauss:<d>:<rows>[:<mean degree>]: linear-Gaussian Erdos-Renyi graph, standardized, mean degree 2 unless given

hardware: PCMB: AMD EPYC 7713 64-Core Processor, 1 core per fit, 1 BLAS thread; fits ran on shared nodes, so the times are indicative | GS, Fast-IAMB, and HITON-PC: AMD EPYC 7713 64-Core Processor, 1 core per fit, 1 BLAS thread; Andrey and bnlearn ran in the same run, one fit after the other, on shared nodes, except GS: its Andrey fits ran after bnlearn's, in separate runs on shared nodes of the same CPU model, so GS's times are indicative | CMB: AMD EPYC 7713 64-Core Processor, 1 core per fit, 1 BLAS thread; CMB, Andrey's PC, and bnlearn ran in the same run, one fit after the other, on shared nodes, so the times are indicative
